title: fullcycle: --dry-run runs the project's build, a lone commands.build.run passes the rebuild check and the cycle deletes the trees before `build all` refuses, and four smaller points
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 by 0115's page agent for `fullcycle`, and driven again by cc at 4c9d5a7 with stubs on PATH. NOT LIVE IN THE FLEET TODAY: every rust estate's build is a handler that answers --help without building (Conflab, Intent, Laksa, Lamplight), and Utilz has no build, so fullcycle refuses there. Six points in lib/cmd/fullcycle, the last shared with clean.

1. `--dry-run` RUNS THE BUILD. _fullcycle_can_rebuild runs `bin/devbin build --help` (lib/cmd/fullcycle:139-141). It is called at :781, before the dry-run branch at :798. A `commands.build.run` receives --help as one more argument (run_command, lib/resolve:948). DRIVEN: with `commands.build.run: scripts/build`, a script that ignores --help, `fullcycle --dry-run` printed "DRY RUN -- nothing below is executed." and the script ran; the file it touches existed afterwards. The usage says --dry-run "executes nothing" (:43).

2. THE SAME PROBE REFUSES A WORKING BUILD. A build whose tool rejects --help fails the probe, and fullcycle refuses: "this project has no build command" (:782). DRIVEN: a script that exits 2 on --help and builds otherwise. `bin/devbin build` exited 0; `fullcycle --force` refused, exit 1.

3. A LONE `commands.build.run` PASSES THE PROBE, AND THE CYCLE DELETES BEFORE ITS BUILD PHASE FAILS. The build phase is `build all` (:105). With no options, `build all` refuses: "has no options to run" (lib/resolve:535). DRIVEN with `commands.build.run: cargo build --release`, where cargo answers --help so the probe passes. `fullcycle --force` removed target/, then printed "phase: build all ... rc=1" and "THE BUILD TREES WERE ALREADY REMOVED AND HAVE NOT BEEN REBUILT". Its remedy line was "Rebuild before doing anything else: bin/devbin build all" (:257, called at :491), the command that had just refused. Exit 1, target/ gone.

4. THE ARTEFACT CHECK CLAIMS A REMOVAL THAT NEVER HAPPENED. When release artefacts are missing it prints "The clean removed release/ and this cycle did not put it back." (:687). The key is `cleaned=1`, which means the clean phase passed, not that it removed anything. DRIVEN: no target/ before the run; the clean phase printed "no removable target/ trees"; a dev-only build option created target/debug; the check printed the sentence. Failing that run is right. The sentence is not.

5. THE PATH WATCH COMPARES A LINK'S TEXT, NOT WHERE IT RESOLVES. _fullcycle_path_links keeps a link only when readlink's text starts with PROJECT_ROOT (:188, and the find pattern at :195). A relative link, and one spelled through /tmp while PROJECT_ROOT is the physical /private/tmp path, are never watched. DRIVEN with three PATH links into target/release: one relative, one spelled through /tmp, one physical.
- clean's own scan named all three.
- fullcycle's header said "watching: 1 PATH symlink(s)".
- After the cycle all three dangled, and "THIS CYCLE DARKENED BINARIES IT DID NOT RESTORE" named only the physical one.

6. TWO PROMPTS, TWO ANSWER SETS. ask_person, behind both clean's prompt and fullcycle's, takes y or Y (lib/helpers:1818). devbin_offer_upgrade takes y, Y, yes and YES (:1888). A person who answers yes to fullcycle is told the cycle was declined.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO:
- (1) to (3): asking whether the cycle can rebuild must not run the build, and must ask about what the build phase will actually run. fullcycle must not call `build all` over a build with no options; vc notes this holds whichever way hv rules on `all`. And the probe must not hand --help to a project's command line.
- (4): say what is true, that the release artefacts are absent after the cycle, without claiming the clean removed them.
- (5): watch a link by where it resolves. clean already computes that, through follow_links.
- (6): one answer set for both prompts, defined once.

PAGES. 0115's fullcycle.md describes (3), (6) and (5) as they are today, at lines 13, 23 and 33, and clean.md does (6) at its prompt section. The fix edits those lines in the same change. It ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling. cc's.

## Resolution

Fixed at 9f9b3b2. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. fullcycle's build and test phases are what those commands run in this project, derived from lib/resolve's own answers (arg_route and command_tier) and run nothing to learn: `<command> all` where there are options to sweep or a handler to hand it to, and the bare `<command>` over a lone command-level run:, whose `all` is refused. So a dry run executes nothing (point 1), a build whose tool refuses --help is a build (point 2), and a lone `commands.build.run` is the build phase rather than `build all` refused after the trees are gone (point 3). A phase the config alone shows cannot run is refused before anything is shown, asked or removed, a reason a line in the dispatcher's own words: nothing behind the command, a run: line with no words, a handler that does not resolve, options every one kept out of `all`, and any option `all` would run that has nothing to run it, whose devbin handler is missing, or whose own run:, or the command-level run: it is handed to, holds no words; and the test phase as the build's. What `all` sweeps is stated once, all_partition in lib/resolve, which run_all and fullcycle both ask, with one sentence, all_excluded_why, for an `all` that would run nothing. The rebuild remedy names the build phase. The artefact check says release/ holds no binary while debug/ does, and claims no removal (point 4). The PATH watch decides each link by where it resolves -- real_path, moved from clean to lib/helpers and shared, for a live link, and a walk through link_step for a dangling one -- and searches a PATH entry that is a link to a directory, where it read a link's text and watched only one spelling (point 5, and critic-shell's W4(i) on 0139). One answer set, is_yes_answer, y or yes in any case, for every question devbin asks (point 6). The pages and docs say each.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD. On a disk that folds case, a PATH link spelled with other letters than the project's directory is not watched; clean's scan shares it. A PATH link outside the project that reaches it only through another linked directory, with the project's name nowhere in its text, is not watched, and a project whose directory name many links hold pays a resolution per candidate. A command line, or an option's, that runs and fails is a failing phase as any other is. 0083's arm over an `all` that runs nothing now holds a refusal before the clean where it held a stop after it.
- REVIEWS. critic-shell's four passes: on v1 (2 critical, 2 warnings, 3 recommendations, 1 style), on v2 (1 warning, 4 recommendations, 3 style), on v2c (1 warning, 4 recommendations, 1 style), and on v2d under vc's convergence rule (0 critical, 0 warnings, no false green, 3 recommendations and 2 style, taken as v2e); each point built or answered, and the commit message names each with the pass that raised it. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-25, approved at v2e on the rulings built as ruled, the drives and the evidence below; the final suite over the landed stack is below.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Each new arm red at its own assertion over cc824b4's code, and each revision's over the code before it; the three that hold behaviour cc824b4 already had are held by mutants. 52 mutants, each against its own arm after every killer ran green on the unmutated tree: 51 killed and one equivalent, a loop guard no reachable path takes.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the six remaining 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on a252178 (0134, 0135, 0145, 0149, 0148, 0150), on a clean checkout built from the six exports (head 55f4c7e, tree 840726e0, the build stack's own tree), 2026-09-26 02:11:38Z to 02:46:47Z: 2040 of 2040 ok, 0 not ok, its 5 skips the declared ones (two no-tty branches, two require_command arms that skip off CI, the case-sensitive rename arm on this case-folding disk); the arms that need real cargo ran. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree.
